links.targetTitle: Amending the Osero Artifact runs a four-stage Root Edit: hol

title: Osero has no defined route for expert review of technically complex Root Edit proposals
content:
A.6.1.1.7.2.2.2.2.1.2.1.2, Root Edit Expert Advisor Review, sits between submission and Facilitator review in the Routine Protocol and contains only a deferral: "A future iteration of the Osero Artifact will specify guidelines for obtaining specialized review of proposals requiring advanced technical or financial analysis."

The placement is the point. The stage is positioned exactly where specialist input would inform the alignment finding, and its emptiness therefore has a concrete effect rather than being a cosmetic gap: complex proposals reach the Facilitator with no defined mechanism for independent expert scrutiny.

This matters disproportionately for Osero specifically. An Agent whose business is credit infrastructure and institutional lending will generate proposals whose alignment turns on financial-structuring questions — exactly the class the missing stage was reserved for.

The interaction with A.6.1.1.7.2.2.2.2.1.2.1.3 is the tension worth recording. The Facilitator's finding is a hard gate with no appeal, and the Facilitator must judge both alignment and operational feasibility. Until the Expert Advisor guidelines exist, that unappealable judgment on technically dense proposals rests on one actor's own expertise.
description: The Expert Advisor Review stage exists as a named but empty step deferred to a future Artifact iteration, leaving the Facilitator as sole judge of advanced technical and financial claims.
